A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain 36 readable pages, including Appendices A–H. Text, equations, figures, tables, and algorithms support a complete comparison.

before.justification: Section 6 reports original synthetic-data and medical-data experiments, with results in Figures 3–4 and Table 1. Appendix G contains further experimental results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments and their outcomes in Section 6 and Appendix G, including estimated treatment effects, confidence intervals, and RMSE results.

M1.justification: The prediction-powered estimator, sample splitting, influence-function calculation, rectifier, and CI construction are unchanged. The RCT extension and Algorithms 1–2 are also retained without procedural changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic confounding scenarios, observational and RCT combinations, MIMIC-III data, and Brazilian COVID-19 data. The additional scenarios in Appendix G are unchanged.

E2.justification: AIPW using D1 only or D2 only remains in the corresponding comparisons. A-TMLE retains the same participation in the RCT comparison and Appendix G robustness and refutation checks.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendices F–G retain the same data generation, preprocessing, splits, model configurations, and evaluation procedures. These include the main synthetic setting n = 200 and N = 5000, sample-size sweeps, and significance levels.

E4.justification: The same analyses test nuisance-model choices, covariate dimensionality and dependence, confounding in D1, propensity estimation, A-TMLE applicability, and dataset sizes. No analysis or supporting evidence is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report experiments across five random seeds, with the same CI reporting, averages, and plotted uncertainty displays. Appendix F.3 and the relevant figure and table captions disclose identical statistical practices.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and Figures 3–14 retain the same results and trends. For example, the proposed method's Table 1 CI widths remain 0.023 for MIMIC-III, 2.341 for COVID-19 by region, and 0.026 by ethnicity.

T1.justification: The assumptions, definitions, Lemma 4.1, Theorems 4.2 and 5.2, and their proofs are unchanged. Appendices B–C and H retain the same mathematical extensions, background, and derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same contributions: prediction-powered ATE confidence intervals from multiple observational datasets, theoretical guarantees, empirical effectiveness, and an extension to RCT plus observational data.

C2.justification: The explanations of CI narrowing, confounding correction, and A-TMLE instability are unchanged. Section 7 retains the same applicability cautions and future directions involving CATE, survival analysis, and language models.

D1.justification: Appendices D and F retain identical pseudocode, preprocessing instructions, regression-model choices, and default-setting disclosures. The code/data availability statement and repository address in footnote 2 are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendices E and H, and the bibliography retain the same cited works and research positioning, including the distinctions from existing PPI methods and A-TMLE.

P1.justification: The running header changes from 'Preprint' to 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025', and the arXiv version/date stamp updates. The substantive prose and section and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: All 14 figures, both tables, and both algorithm displays retain their structure and placement. Captions, axes, legends, graphical content, and body layout match; the header wording update does not reorganize the layout.

improvement.justification: v2 updates publication labels while retaining the scientific exposition, methods, proofs, experimental evidence, and reproducibility information throughout the main paper and Appendices A–H. These changes provide no meaningful gain or loss in clarity, rigor, or evidential support.
